samples.question: This picture contains one dark filament: a single thin unbroken line that wanders back and forth across the whole canvas and never touches itself. One end of the filament carries a red hub, and inside that hub a short blue bar points from the hub's centre towards its rim; the direction of that bar is the direction the pointer holds at the start of the walk, read as a compass on the page, with north up, east right, south down and west left. The other end of the filament is capped by a small dark square. Small coloured square tabs are welded to one side of the filament along its length: an orange tab turns the pointer one quarter turn clockwise, and a teal tab mirrors the pointer left to right, so east becomes west and west becomes east while north and south are unchanged. Walk the filament from the red hub to the capped end, following the line itself rather than the left-to-right or top-to-bottom order of the page, and apply each tab at the moment you pass it; a tab acts only once and the tabs act in the order they are met. Every grey ring and grey dash lying away from the filament is inert decoration. In which compass direction does the pointer point when the capped end is reached? Answer with one of north, east, south or west.
